theme: A research lab: experiments, equipment, people
facts: The confocal microscope is booked through the shared calendar in two-hour blocks.
The -80 freezer is checked for temperature every Monday.

Experiments follow a preregistered protocol that is stored in the lab wiki before any data are collected. Every run records the reagent lot number, the operator, and the plate layout. Negative results are logged in the same format as positive results. Changes to the protocol after data collection must be marked as exploratory in the analysis notebook.
The plate reader is calibrated with a standard set every two weeks.
Dr. Elena Vasquez is the principal investigator and signs off on all grant reports.

Raw data must be stored in the shared drive under the project folder, and never on personal laptops. Analysis scripts are version-controlled in the lab repository. Each dataset gets a README with the date, instrument, and processing steps. Files are kept for seven years after publication, as the funder requires.
Ravi manages the lab's inventory and places all purchase orders.
Kofi is the postdoc who runs the sequencing pipeline and trains new students on it.

Lab meeting happens every Wednesday at ten in the seminar room, and each member presents one slide of progress. Presentations should include the question, the result, and the next experiment. Anyone who misses lab meeting must send their slide by Tuesday night. Journal club rotates on alternate Fridays.
Ines is a third-year PhD student.
Equipment bookings must be cancelled at least a day ahead, or they count as no-shows.

Lab safety training must be renewed every year, and new members cannot enter the cell culture room until it is complete. Gloves and goggles are required in all wet labs. Chemical waste goes into labeled containers that are picked up every second Tuesday. Accidents must be reported to Ravi within the same day.
Ines writes thesis chapters on set weekdays and avoids meetings then.
The lab's grant renewal is due in March.
Samples must be labeled with the date, initials, and sample ID using the lab printer.

The lab's shared computing cluster is available overnight, but jobs longer than 48 hours must be checkpointed. Users must request a quota increase from Kofi before submitting large jobs. Scripts that consume more than the quota are killed without warning. Results are copied back to the project folder, not left on the cluster.
Ravi is the emergency contact and answers his phone during working hours.

Authorship on papers follows the CRediT taxonomy, and the first author must draft the outline before any writing starts. The PI reviews the final draft, and co-authors have one week to comment. Preprints are allowed only after the internal review is complete. Conference abstracts are not counted as publications.
Ines gets priority on the plate reader for her assays.
The lab uses electronic lab notebooks, and paper notes must be scanned within a week.

Visitors must sign the visitor log and wear a lab coat when in the wet lab. Guests cannot operate any equipment without a trained member present. Visitor access is granted by the PI only, and it expires after thirty days. Photographs of the lab are allowed only in common areas.
Kofi takes his vacation in August, and his out-of-office email forwards to Ravi.
Spare reagents are stored on the third shelf of the cold room.

New projects need a one-page plan that lists the question, the expected outcome, the equipment, and the budget. The plan is reviewed at the next lab meeting. If a project is dropped, the data and notes are archived in the project folder. Students must update the plan every semester with a short status note.
